newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re to split shares 10 for 1.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re to split shares 10 for 1.

text.p: German insurance group Munich Re said on Friday it will split its bearer shares and registered shares in a ratio of 10 for one with effect from August 18.

Every Munich Re registered share with a nominal value of 100 marks, of which 50 marks is paid up, will be converted into 10 registered shares with a nominal value of 10 marks each, of which five marks is paid up, the company said in a statement.
The nominal value of Munich Re bearer shares will also be divided by 10 and will in future amount to five marks.
"Munich Re expects this stock split to further improve the conditions for trading in its shares," the statement said.
The move means Munich Re shares will trade at 10 percent of their current price. Based on the price at 1300 GMT, Munich Re's share price would fall to 593 marks from 5,930 marks.
The step was made possible by the inclusion of Munich Re's registered shares in the central German securities depositary, enabling them to be included in the giro transfer system, Munich Re said.
"This will make for cheaper custody and simpler trading of the registered shares, which account for more than 95 percent of Munich Re's share capital."
